what_happened: Dispatch's Gap 3 description (the WSL sync-notice activation entry with the lingering warning) describes packages/sapience-flake/modules/sapience.nix (the non-live fork, added in commit 20715ff), not the live modules/home/services/sapience.nix, which has zero WSL/linger references. 'KEEP the existing activation notice' cannot be executed literally against the live file.

Gap 1's tokenFile already flows through the full sap_token_clean/sap_token_ok/server-verification gauntlet with no code change needed -- just secrets wiring. Gap 2's sourceDirs option description already contains option (b)'s exact required wording ('Run it by hand; nothing here is scheduled and activation never ingests anything'), so the code-side acceptance criterion is already met; only the reasoning record and an (a)-vs-(b) decision remain for planning.

Acceptance Criterion 4 requires verifying 'loginctl show-user <name> --property=Linger' after a nixos-rebuild switch, but a carried memory record in this task's own dispatch states sudo is categorically denied in this harness, so an agent cannot run nixos-rebuild switch to make or verify the linger grant take effect.

Dispatch GAP 3 instructed 'KEEP the existing activation notice' in the live module modules/home/services/sapience.nix, but a re-grep for linger/WSL/systemd=true across that file, modules/system/ and hosts/ returns zero matches: the notice (sapienceWslSyncNotice) exists only in the non-live packages/sapience-flake fork. Plan resolves this by authoring a NEW narrowed notice in the live module rather than porting fork code, and records the divergence.

GAP 2's (a)-vs-(b) design question was settled decisively by reading vendor source rather than weighing the dispatch's framing: ~/.sapience/sapience_adddir.py:413-420 requires a TTY confirmation or --yes before reading any file, so an activation-time adddir call is either a decorative no-op or an unattended forced upload. That is a stronger argument for (b) than the ledger-cost framing the dispatch supplied.

Team lead overrode the plan's Decision 4 / Phase 6 Closure rule: instead of closing Phase 6 as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] after running agent-executable verification, left it [BLOCKED] (open) and deferred the full operator sequence (sops edit, two sudo nixos-rebuild switch runs, loginctl check, real-token sapience-bootstrap) to the user, printing the exact command sequence in the summary.

statix's repeated-key lint ('Avoid repeated keys in attribute sets') fires at 3 occurrences of a top-level 'secrets."name" = {...};' pattern in modules/system/secrets.nix (2 occurrences pass; adding a third naive entry failed nix flake check's checks.x86_64-linux.statix). Fixed by restructuring all three entries into one nested 'secrets = { "a" = ...; "b" = ...; "c" = ...; };' attrset, matching statix's own suggested fix.

Phase 1's token-quoting grep verification command as literally specified in the plan (grep -nE 'tokenFile *= *[^"]' home.nix) was non-discriminating due to a quantifier/character-class interaction (the space before the opening quote satisfies [^"]); caught this by running the same pattern against the already-correct apiKeyFile precedent line and seeing the same false-positive match, then substituted a corrected single-space form that actually discriminates quoted from unquoted assignments.

phase 6: Acceptance Criterion 4 (loginctl Linger=yes after a system switch); AC2's live half (prompt-free sapience-bootstrap against a real /run/secrets/sapience_token); AC5's system-switch no-op half | goal: Apply the real Sapience token via sops and run sudo nixos-rebuild switch (twice) to give all six acceptance criteria live evidence, per the user's recorded decision. | tried: Ran every agent-executable substitute: nix flake check, the scoped agent-system gate, two consecutive home-manager switch runs (confirmed no-op and token-leak-free), and a full scratchpad-isolated demonstration of the non-interactive tokenFile bootstrap path against a placeholder value. | failed: sudo is structurally denied in this harness (confirmed by prior-session memory and the team lead's own instruction), and the real Sapience token must never reach an agent. Both are outside what this dispatch can do; the team lead directed that this be left for the user rather than closed as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS].

orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh: a 'partial with unresolved blocker(s); needs human' verdict charges the task to the run's failed_tasks[] in the multi-state file. The all-terminal check (section (b)) then tests in_json_array failed_tasks BEFORE/independently of task_has_forced_phase, so a subsequent --force-phases implement call reusing the SAME session_id is silently swallowed and misreported as stop.reason=all_terminal ('Every task is terminal, failed, or excluded') for a task whose state.json status is plainly 'partial' (non-terminal). The forcing flag is documented as the admission override for exactly this case, so the interaction defeats its purpose and the message actively misleads. Workaround: mint a fresh session_id, which resets the per-run multi-state file. Observed with task 144 resuming after its Phase 6 operator checkpoint was satisfied by the user.

Closed Phase 6's AC5 second-switch no-op proof without sudo: readlink -f /run/current-system and a non-activating nix build of the same host's nixosConfigurations.<host>.config.system.build.toplevel resolved to the identical store path, proving convergence without running the literal (sudo-gated) second switch.
